items.title: Bruce Johnstone interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2013
items.q: The rhythm section was great. It was Neils Henning was playing bass, and Kenny Drew was playing piano. And they knew what Dexter was doing. And Kenny Drew just kind of rolled his eyes. And he walked me through it.

ctx.x: Were you hearing Coltrane and the sort of avante garde, well sort of progressive stuff that was going on in the sixties? Were you hearing it and listening to it?

I was listening to it. I admired Coltrane. I thought it was absolutely fantastic. But I didn’t want to copy him because it was so unique and I didn’t want to make a pale image of what Coltrane was doing. A lot of what he was doing was beyond my understanding at that point. And I had needed to just sit down and listen to him. I was also familiar with Albert Ayler, who was just ripping and tearing. But I was more back in the tradition. I was kind of steeped in the Lester Young style of playing. And one of my…

played with Bill Evans, recorded with Dexter, and he’s still one of the best drummers I’ve ever heard. So I kind of stumbled into this scene by having the nerve to go up and ask Dexter if I’d get to sit in with him.
